objective: Add a transport-neutral Cloud IaC OpenTofu module-registry HTTP handler boundary that converts oya-http-middleware-kernel HttpRequest values into OpenTofu-compatible discovery, versions, and download JSON HttpResponse values from the existing runtime dispatcher while preserving no live HTTP listener/server, deployed endpoint, auth runtime, persistence, signing, SLSA/VSA, tofu plan/apply, provider runtime, FD-001 tenant workload hosting, or cloud provisioning claims.

best_practice_sources.what_it_establishes: OpenTofu clients discover service base URLs through /.well-known/terraform.json, including modules.v1.
Module registry versions endpoint produces application/json; download endpoint may return a JSON body containing location, and OpenTofu prioritizes response body over X-Terraform-Get if both exist.
Module source location strings identify reusable module packages; serving credentials/provider execution are separate concerns.

implemented_claims: Added a transport-neutral HTTP handler boundary to oya-cloud-iac-runtime using oya-http-middleware-kernel HttpRequest/HttpResponse.
Rendered OpenTofu service discovery as a modules.v1 JSON document.
Rendered versions responses as a single module entry with semver-ordered version objects from the existing API DTO boundary.
Rendered download responses as a JSON location body accepted by the OpenTofu module registry protocol.
Mapped wrong methods, unknown routes, missing module versions, forbidden surfaces, invalid request metadata, and unexpected GET bodies to explicit HTTP statuses without starting a server.
explicit_non_claims: no live HTTP listener or Hyper server composition
no registry publish path or object-store serving
no request authentication or Cedar runtime integration beyond injected in-process authorization metadata checks
no module signing or Sigstore/cosign execution
no SLSA or VSA attestation generation
no provider runtime, provider API calls, provider credentials, or cloud provisioning
no FD-001 microservice dogfood tenant workload hosting or production tenant workload evidence
false_green_findings_closed: Closed the gap between in-process route/API dispatch and HTTP response compatibility by adding a transport-neutral handler with exact JSON response tests.
Avoided treating the handler as a deployed module registry service: no Hyper import, no socket binding, no listener, no deployed endpoint.
Avoided fake auth/runtime claims: authorization remains injected metadata checked by the existing API boundary, not live Cedar/auth middleware.
known_gaps: Full ./bin/oya verify --ci-required is not claimed by this ChangeSet; repo-wide unrelated blockers remain outside this Cloud IaC slice.

Cloud IaC still needs future slices for actual HTTP listener composition, live service discovery and module versions/download endpoints, registry publish path, object-store serving, authentication/Cedar runtime integration, database adapter, module signing/Sigstore/cosign, SLSA attestations, independent provider provenance/VSA verification, tofu tests, plan/apply evidence, provider-resource-complete modules, and live GitOps/provider integration evidence.

FD-001 remains the master-plan product delivery goal and Oyatie Cloud must later prove itself by hosting FD-001 microservices as tenant workloads; this ChangeSet provides no tenant-workload dogfood evidence.
Concurrent unrelated application-shell and other agent work exists in the worktree; this ChangeSet does not claim or modify those surfaces.
The complementary /Users/jasonlee/Developer/source/plan files informed sequencing only and are not treated as source-of-truth implementation evidence.

findings: The handler is a small adapter over existing runtime dispatch and manual JSON rendering; no framework or server complexity added.
Moves the substrate one step closer to an internal module registry service while preserving that deployed/runtime/cloud claims remain false until later evidence exists.
FD-001 tenant workload dogfood hosting remains future proof of substrate readiness, not a claim here.
Tests cover wrong methods, unknown routes, missing versions, forbidden surfaces, and unexpected GET bodies.
Future Hyper adapter composition can wrap the typed handler because it implements the repo-local Handler trait.
No new external dependencies; focused tests, fmt, check, clippy, architecture, and run-all gates passed.
Chose transport-neutral HttpRequest/HttpResponse handler instead of a live Hyper server to lock response semantics before listener/deployment work.
The handler rejects unexpected request bodies, preserves API authorization checks, and returns low-detail error codes without echoing path captures or secrets.
Manual JSON construction over bounded in-memory DTOs only; no network, filesystem, provider, or OpenTofu execution added.
Manifest, tasks, evidence, and audit rows encode local-only HTTP-handler scope and explicit non-claims.
HTTP response shapes follow official OpenTofu service discovery and module registry protocol docs, including JSON download location response.
Manifest scope, tasks/plan, tasks/todo, multispectrum evidence, and audit-chain entries updated.
The handler exposes status/body semantics that a future Hyper listener can serve; no service operations are claimed.
Oya VCS claim used before source changes; no raw git/gh; architecture-boundaries role constraints preserved.
Official OpenTofu docs establish response semantics; repo-local evidence distinguishes handler boundary from live endpoint evidence.
Explicitly excludes live endpoints, auth runtime, persistence, signing/SLSA, provider runtime, plan/apply, cloud provisioning, full verify, and FD-001 tenant workload hosting.
